species.name: Yelloweye rockfish
features: Bright orange to orange-red body, often with yellow tints
Bright golden-yellow eye: the giveaway
Adults have rough, raspy ridges on top of the head
Juveniles have two white stripes along the side and white-edged fins
Usually deep (40+ fathoms), though found shallower up north

lookalikes.name: Canary rockfish
lookalikes.how: Canary has gray mottling with three orange stripes across the head and a smooth head; its eye isn't bright yellow.

lookalikes.name: Vermilion rockfish
lookalikes.how: Vermilion is red with gray mottling and rough scales under the lower jaw; eye is reddish, not yellow.

species.regs: No retention anywhere in California, any time. Release quickly with a descending device.

species.name: Cowcod
features: Very large head and big mouth
Spiny dorsal fin with very deep notches between spines
Pinkish to tan-orange or reddish, often with 4–5 faint dark vertical bars
One of the largest rockfish (to ~3 ft); deep water, mostly Southern California

lookalikes.name: Bocaccio
lookalikes.how: Bocaccio is long and slender with the lower jaw jutting past the upper; cowcod is deep-bodied with a huge head.

lookalikes.name: Vermilion rockfish
lookalikes.how: Vermilion is bright red with gray mottling and lacks the deeply notched dorsal fin.

species.regs: No retention anywhere in California, any time.

species.name: Quillback rockfish
features: Brown to black body with yellow-orange speckling on the head and front of the body
Very tall spiny dorsal fin with deep notches (the 'quills'), often yellowish
Pale yellow-orange area behind the head
Mostly Northern and Central California

lookalikes.name: Copper rockfish
lookalikes.how: Copper has a pale stripe along the rear two-thirds of the lateral line, a white belly, and a lower dorsal fin without deep notches.

lookalikes.name: China rockfish
lookalikes.how: China has one bold yellow stripe running from the dorsal fin down along the side to the tail.

species.regs: No retention anywhere in California, any time.

species.name: Bronzespotted rockfish
features: Orange to pinkish-orange body covered with bronze to dark spots on the back and sides
Large head; deep water (usually 40–200+ fathoms)
Mainly Southern California and offshore banks

lookalikes.name: Starry rockfish
lookalikes.how: Starry is red-orange with many small white spots and a few larger white blotches, not bronze spots.

species.regs: No retention anywhere in California, any time.
species.photo_credit: NOAA NMFS SWFSC ROV Team, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Blue rockfish
features: Blue-gray to blue-black with darker mottling and blotches
Small mouth: upper jaw reaches only to about the middle of the eye
Rear edge of the anal fin is straight or slanted
Very common in kelp and over shallow reefs

lookalikes.name: Deacon rockfish
lookalikes.how: Deacon is lighter and more evenly gray-blue with little mottling. Both count the same under the rules.

lookalikes.name: Black rockfish
lookalikes.how: Black has a bigger mouth (jaw reaches the back of the eye), dark spots on the spiny dorsal fin, and a rounded anal fin.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Claire Fackler, CINMS, NOAA., public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Deacon rockfish
features: Pale blue-gray, more uniform than blue rockfish, often with a light belly
Small mouth and straight-edged anal fin like the blue rockfish
Common from Central California north

lookalikes.name: Blue rockfish
lookalikes.how: Blue is darker with distinct mottling. Same bag rules, so the difference doesn't change what you can keep.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Black rockfish
features: Black to gray-black back fading to a whitish belly
Large mouth: upper jaw reaches to the back of the eye or beyond
Dark spots on the spiny dorsal fin
Rounded rear edge on the anal fin
More common north of Point Conception and especially north of SF

lookalikes.name: Blue rockfish
lookalikes.how: Blue has a small mouth, mottled blue-gray color, and a straight-edged anal fin.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: User Sabine's Sunbird on en.wikipedia, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Gopher rockfish
features: Olive-brown to reddish-brown body with pale pinkish or white blotches
Stocky, big-headed reef fish
Often in rocky crevices in 30–120 ft

lookalikes.name: Black-and-yellow rockfish
lookalikes.how: Same shape and pattern, but black with bright yellow blotches instead of brown with pale blotches.

lookalikes.name: Kelp rockfish
lookalikes.how: Kelp is evenly mottled tan-brown without crisp pale blotches.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Black-and-yellow rockfish
features: Black to dark olive body with bold bright-yellow blotches
Stocky, gopher-shaped
Shallow rocky reef, often very close to shore

lookalikes.name: Gopher rockfish
lookalikes.how: Gopher has brown with pale/pinkish blotches instead of black with yellow.

lookalikes.name: China rockfish
lookalikes.how: China has one long yellow stripe along the side rather than blotches.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Claire Fackler, NOAA National Marine Sanctuaries, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Kelp rockfish
features: Mottled olive-brown to tan with darker blotches, fins mottled too
Slimmer than gopher; often rests head-down in kelp
Spines are venomous: handle carefully

lookalikes.name: Grass rockfish
lookalikes.how: Grass is darker green-olive, chunkier, with very short, thick gill rakers.

lookalikes.name: Brown rockfish
lookalikes.how: Brown has a dark brown blotch on the gill cover.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Grass rockfish
features: Dark green to olive with mottling
Very stocky with a big head
Very shallow: tidepools, jetties and kelp beds
Short, stubby gill rakers

lookalikes.name: Kelp rockfish
lookalikes.how: Kelp rockfish is slimmer and tan-brown rather than dark green.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: China rockfish
features: Black to blue-black with yellow and white mottling
One bold yellow stripe from the spiny dorsal fin down along the lateral line to the tail
Rocky reefs, often in crevices

lookalikes.name: Quillback rockfish (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Quillback has no single long stripe; it has yellow-orange speckles on the front half and a tall, deeply notched dorsal fin.

lookalikes.name: Black-and-yellow rockfish
lookalikes.how: Black-and-yellow has blotches, not a stripe.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Lt. John Crofts, NOAA Corps., public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Copper rockfish
features: Copper, orange-brown or dark brown with pinkish-orange blotches
Pale or white stripe along the rear two-thirds of the lateral line
White belly
Dark bands radiating back from the eye

lookalikes.name: Quillback rockfish (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Quillback has a much taller, deeply notched dorsal fin and yellow-orange speckles on the head, and lacks the pale lateral-line stripe.

lookalikes.name: Brown rockfish
lookalikes.how: Brown has a dark blotch on the gill cover and no white belly.

species.regs: Only 1 copper rockfish per person, within the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Olive rockfish
features: Streamlined, bass-like body
Olive-brown back with a row of pale spots under the dorsal fin
Fins tinged olive-yellow
Mid-water around kelp and reefs

lookalikes.name: Yellowtail rockfish
lookalikes.how: Yellowtail has a bright yellow tail, orange-brown flecks on the scales, and lives deeper on the shelf.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Yellowtail rockfish
features: Gray-brown to olive back with orange-brown flecks on the scales
Bright yellow tail and fins
Schools in mid-water over the shelf, usually deeper than olive rockfish

lookalikes.name: Olive rockfish
lookalikes.how: Olive's fins are olive-yellow, not bright yellow, and it has pale spots along its back.

species.regs: Shelf rockfish; part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Linda Snook, Cordell Bank National Marine Sanctuary, via NOAA Fisheries

species.name: Vermilion / sunset rockfish
features: Bright red to red-orange body with gray mottling on the sides
Rough scales under the lower jaw
Fins red, often edged in black (especially young fish)
Vermilion and sunset rockfish look identical and are counted together

lookalikes.name: Yelloweye rockfish (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Yelloweye has a bright yellow eye and a raspy head.

lookalikes.name: Canary rockfish
lookalikes.how: Canary is orange on gray with three orange stripes across the head.

species.regs: 2 vermilion/sunset combined per person (4 in the Northern area), within the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Victor Simon, NOAA/NMFS/NWFSC/FRAMD/MF, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Canary rockfish
features: Bright orange mottling over a gray background
Three orange stripes across the head
Orange fins; young fish have a black spot on the rear spiny dorsal fin
Smooth head, no rasps

lookalikes.name: Yelloweye rockfish (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Yelloweye has a bright yellow eye, a raspy head, and is more uniformly orange-red without gray.

lookalikes.name: Vermilion rockfish
lookalikes.how: Vermilion is deep red, not orange, and has rough scales under the jaw.

species.regs: 2 canary per person, within the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Bocaccio
features: Long, slender body
Very large mouth; lower jaw sticks out past the upper
Olive-brown to reddish; young fish often have dark spots
Shelf depths, often over deep reefs

lookalikes.name: Cowcod (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Cowcod is deep-bodied with a huge head and deeply notched dorsal fin.

species.regs: Shelf rockfish; part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Starry rockfish
features: Red-orange body covered with many small white spots
3–5 larger white blotches along the back
Deeper reefs on the shelf

lookalikes.name: Bronzespotted rockfish (never keep)
lookalikes.how: Bronzespotted has bronze/dark spots, not white spots.

species.regs: Shelf rockfish; part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Jodi Pirtle. Credit: NOAA/CBNMS., public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Brown rockfish
features: Light brown with darker brown mottling
Dark brown blotch on the upper gill cover
Common in bays, harbors and around piers

lookalikes.name: Copper rockfish
lookalikes.how: Copper has a white belly and pale lateral-line stripe, and no gill-cover blotch.

lookalikes.name: Kelp rockfish
lookalikes.how: Kelp lacks the gill-cover blotch.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Treefish
features: Yellow to olive body with 5–6 bold black vertical bars
Pinkish-red lips
Shallow rocky reefs, often in crevices

lookalikes.name: Black-and-yellow rockfish
lookalikes.how: Black-and-yellow has irregular blotches, not neat vertical bars, and no pink lips.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.

species.name: Lingcod
features: Long body and huge mouth full of sharp, fang-like teeth
Mottled brown, gray or greenish (flesh is sometimes blue-green, which is fine to eat)
Long dorsal fin with a notch about halfway

lookalikes.name: Kelp greenling
lookalikes.how: Greenlings are much smaller with a small mouth and no fangs.

species.regs: 2 per person, 22 in. minimum total length. Fillets at least 14 in. with skin on.

species.name: Cabezon
features: Big, scaleless sculpin with a very large head
Fleshy flap (cirrus) above each eye and on the snout
Mottled red, brown or green
Don't eat the roe: it's toxic

lookalikes.name: Lingcod
lookalikes.how: Lingcod has scales, fangs and a slimmer body, and no fleshy flaps over the eyes.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Lt. John Crofts, NOAA Corps., public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Kelp greenling
features: Small mouth and several lateral lines along the side
Males: gray-brown with bright blue spots on the head and front
Females: covered in small reddish-brown to golden spots
Kelp beds and shallow reefs

lookalikes.name: Rock greenling
lookalikes.how: Rock greenling has rougher scales and is usually marked with bold red blotches. Same bag rules.

lookalikes.name: Lingcod
lookalikes.how: Lingcod has a huge mouth with fangs.

species.regs: Part of the 10-fish RCG bag.
species.photo_credit: Steve Lonhart / NOAA MBNMS, public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: California halibut
features: Large flatfish; eyes can be on either side
Large mouth: the jaw extends past the rear of the eye, with sharp teeth
Lateral line arches high over the pectoral fin
Sandy bottoms, bays and along the beach

lookalikes.name: Pacific halibut
lookalikes.how: Pacific halibut is always right-eyed, has a smaller mouth (not past the eye), a gentle lateral-line arch, and a crescent-shaped tail.

lookalikes.name: Sanddabs
lookalikes.how: Sanddabs are small, left-eyed, with a straight lateral line and a small mouth.

species.regs: 22 in. minimum. Bag is 5 south of Point Sur, 3 north of Point Sur.

species.name: Pacific halibut
features: Very large, right-eyed flatfish (eyes on the dark right side)
Mouth reaches only to about the front of the eye
Tail is crescent-shaped (concave)
Mostly north of Point Arena, but caught along the Central Coast

lookalikes.name: California halibut
lookalikes.how: California halibut has a big toothy mouth past the eye and a high arch in the lateral line.

species.regs: 1 fish per day; quota-managed season. Only one line with two hooks when angling.

species.name: Pacific sanddab
features: Small, left-eyed flatfish (usually under 12 in.)
Light brown with dull orange or dark speckles
Straight lateral line, small mouth

lookalikes.name: California halibut (juvenile)
lookalikes.how: Young halibut have a large toothy mouth and a strongly arched lateral line.

species.regs: Open year-round at all depths; see the general rules for limits.

species.name: California sheephead
features: Males: black head and tail with a red-pink middle and a white chin
Females: mostly pink to red
Big buck teeth for crushing urchins and crabs
Rocky reefs, mostly Southern California but up to the Central Coast
species.regs: 2 per person, 12 in. minimum. Boat anglers have a season; shore and divers year-round.

species.name: White seabass
features: Silvery body with a blue-gray to bronze back
Raised ridge along the middle of the belly
Young fish have dark vertical bars
Lower jaw slightly longer than upper

lookalikes.name: Juvenile seabass vs. croakers
lookalikes.how: Undersize seabass are often confused with croakers. If it's barred and under 28 in., release it.

species.regs: 28 in. minimum. 3 per day (1 per day south of Point Conception from Mar 15–Jun 15).

species.name: Barred surfperch
features: Silvery body with brassy to olive vertical bars and spots on the sides
The classic sandy-beach perch

lookalikes.name: Redtail surfperch
lookalikes.how: Redtail has reddish tail and fins and needs to be at least 10½ in.

lookalikes.name: Calico surfperch
lookalikes.how: Calico has broken reddish-brown bars and spots.

species.regs: 20 surfperch combined per day, no more than 10 of one species.

species.name: Redtail surfperch
features: Silvery with faint reddish-brown bars
Reddish to pink tail and fins
Mostly Central and Northern California beaches

lookalikes.name: Barred surfperch
lookalikes.how: Barred has brassy bars and yellowish (not red) fins.

species.regs: 10½ in. minimum, within the 20-fish surfperch limit.

species.name: Striped seaperch
features: Copper-orange body with bright blue horizontal stripes
Blue streaks on the head
Rocky shores, jetties and kelp

lookalikes.name: Rubberlip seaperch
lookalikes.how: Rubberlip has thick white-pink lips and no blue stripes.

species.regs: Within the 20-fish surfperch limit.
species.photo_credit: Dr. Dwayne Meadows, NOAA/NMFS/OPR., public domain (Wikimedia Commons)

species.name: Dungeness crab
features: Purplish-brown to tan shell, widest at the last (10th) point
Claws white-tipped, not black
Measured straight across the back, in front of the points

lookalikes.name: Red rock crab
lookalikes.how: Rock crabs have black-tipped claws and a shell that's widest in the middle. Different size and bag limits.

species.regs: 10 per day, 5¾ in. minimum. Season and trap rules change often; check the Rules tab.

species.name: Red rock crab
features: Brick-red shell on top
Heavy claws with black tips
Rocky areas, jetties and bays

lookalikes.name: Dungeness crab
lookalikes.how: Dungeness has white-tipped claws and a lighter purplish-brown shell.

lookalikes.name: Yellow and brown rock crabs
lookalikes.how: Same rules: all rock crab species share the 4 in. minimum and 35 bag.

species.regs: All rock crab species: 35 per day, 4 in. minimum.
